payload.title: The tenant-scoping adapter records crossTenant on every entity-bound call but applies it only to repository reads, so unscoped writes and raw queries on per-tenant tables (routed into the tenant's own schema by search_path) are emitted as findings although premise 1 of the rule excludes per-tenant tables, and the EntityManager change added three more.
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/tenant-scoping-adapter.ts:306-316 (the suppression conditions do not include crossTenant)
tools/aria-adapters/tenant-scoping-adapter.ts:343-345 (the placement gate is applied to REPOSITORY_READ_METHODS only)
tools/aria-adapters/tenant-scoping-adapter.ts:385-393 (the docstring states writes and raw queries do not come through the gate)
tools/aria-adapters/tenant-scoping-adapter.tool.json:39-41 (premise 1 excludes a per-tenant table that search_path routes into the tenant's schema)
tools/aria-adapters/tenant-scoping-adapter.test.ts:533-544 (the test pins per-tenant write and raw-query findings as still flagged)
apps/sensor-service/src/automation/automation.service.ts:359 (manager.delete on ProgramVariable inside a tenant-scoped service)
apps/sensor-service/src/automation/entities/program-variable.entity.ts:63 (the entity declares no schema, so it is a per-tenant table)
payload.rule_violated: The contract of tenant_repository_unscoped_read (premise 1) and the schema-per-tenant rule in CLAUDE.md (per-tenant tables omit schema so search_path routes them); a detector must not emit what its own premise refutes.
payload.notes: In the default run, with the read gate closed, manager.delete(ProgramVariable, { programId: id }) at automation.service.ts:359 and the second delete at :808 are reported as tenant_repository_unscoped_read (severity high, confidence 0.82), although the table lives in the tenant's own schema and premise 1 says such a table is not a defect; the seven repository-form per-tenant write findings in sensor have the same profile. The adapter already holds the deciding fact (crossTenant false on those observations) and does not use it for writes. The parenthetical 'or one keyed by tenantId' in premise 1 also matches every per-tenant table here, so the premise contradicts itself. Close condition: Apply boundary.crossTenant to writes and raw queries as well (a per-tenant table is not a finding), reword premise 1 so the tenantId clause cannot re-admit per-tenant tables, flip the two 'still flagged' test rows, and add a pin that no default-run finding targets an entity whose crossTenant is false. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 4). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
